- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥1.0) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly, especially in early horizon.
- When sentiment is consistently negative (≤-1.0), model underestimates; adjust upward, particularly if recent price is falling sharply.
- Model often overshoots after sharp price spikes (e.g., +10%+ in 3-5 days), especially if sentiment was bullish; apply downward correction in next 5-7 days.
- If sentiment shifts from bullish to bearish mid-horizon, model fails to adjust; reduce forecast slope or add early mean-reversion bias.
- Model underestimates mean-reversion in 10-15 day horizons when sentiment is neutral or mixed; add 2-3% upward bias for 10-day forecasts if sentiment is 0.0.
- For 30-day forecasts, model often misses bottoming or toping; if sentiment is bearish, add 5-10% upward bias to avoid underestimating rebound.
- If sentiment is volatile (alternating +1/-1), model overfits short-term noise; smooth forecast by averaging last 3-5 days’ sentiment-weighted price.
